topic_title: Understand and use linear regression models

mission.display_title: Fit a linear regression in software and interpret the output
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to use appropriate software to fit a linear regression model and interpret the output: inference on the slope, measures of goodness of fit, prediction of mean or individual response with confidence limits, and residual checks of suitability. Without pretending variable selection (4.1.5) is finished.
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will force the candidate to read software output as evidence (slope inference, GOF, prediction limits, residual checks) and refuse treating variable-selection shopping as today's LO.
mission.educational_intent: Produce a cognitive move from hand least squares to software-mediated fit, inference, prediction, and residual diagnostics under CMP.
mission.learning_objective: Use of appropriate software to fit a linear regression model to a data set and interpret the output: Perform statistical inference on the slope parameter; Describe the use of measures of goodness of fit of a linear regression model; Use a fitted linear relationship to predict a mean response or an individual response with confidence limits; Use residuals to check the suitability and validity of a linear regression model
mission.concept_focus: Software fit → slope inference → GOF measures → mean vs individual prediction limits → residual checks.
mission.prior_bridge: Yesterday you obtained least squares estimates for the simple linear model (4.1.3). Today practises software fit and interpretation of that fitted relationship.
mission.why_now: 4.1.4 is contiguous after least squares. Examiners expect software output literacy. Not GUI tourism and not jumping to selection theatre.
mission.expected_benefit: You will be able to interpret a fitted linear regression: slope inference, GOF, prediction limits, and residual checks.
mission.explainability: Assigned as Campaign Nu Day 4 because Continuity Front law keeps variable selection as the final Learning day.
success_criteria: Closed-book, name the four interpretation moves in 4.1.4 (inference, GOF, prediction limits, residual checks).
Distinguish mean-response vs individual-response prediction intervals.
Refuse one 'I picked the best subset today' variable-selection claim.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.1.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes slope inference, goodness-of-fit use, mean versus individual prediction limits, and residual checks after a linear fit?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Slope inference, GOF, prediction limits, and residual checks are all required after a fit. Residuals are not optional after significance, and the two interval types differ in width.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Slope SE and inference; GOF; prediction wider than mean interval; residuals check validity.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating residuals as optional or collapsing GOF to R-squared alone.

choices.label: Report the slope estimate with its standard error and inference under the model. Goodness-of-fit summarises how well the linear relationship describes the data. A prediction interval for a new observation is typically wider than a mean-response interval because it adds residual variance. Residuals check suitability and validity of the linear model.
After a significant slope, residual plots are optional because significance already proves the model is valid.
Mean-response and individual-response intervals are identical for a new x-star because both target E[Y | x-star].
Goodness-of-fit means adjusted R-squared alone; slope inference and prediction limits are not part of software fit output.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.1.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. After fitting Y = β₀ + β₁ x in software you see β̂₁, SE(β̂₁), R-squared, and residual plots. For a new x-star, which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Distinguish mean versus individual prediction; refuse selection.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Mean interval targets the conditional mean; prediction adds observation noise. Variable selection and optional residuals are misconceptions.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Mean interval for E[Y | x-star]; prediction wider; refuse selection-as-fit and optional residuals.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Accepting variable selection as finishing fit, or treating residuals as optional after significance.

choices.label: A mean-response interval covers E[Y | x-star]; a prediction interval covers a new observation and is typically wider (adds residual variance). Running best-subset selection is separate from post-fit inference; slope inference, GOF, prediction limits, and residual checks are all required after a fit.
Running best-subset variable selection finishes software fit and inference for this model.
Because the slope is significant, residual plots are optional diagnostic theatre.
The mean-response interval and prediction interval for x-star are the same width because both estimate E[Y | x-star] only.
